definitions.explanation: Work that is hired and paid on a daily basis, without a long-term contract.
A person who works on a day-to-day basis, typically in construction or manual labor. Can carry connotations of precarious employment.

examples.japanese: {日雇|ひやと}いで{働|はたら}いている。
examples.english: I work as a day laborer.

examples.japanese: {日雇|ひやと}いの{仕事|しごと}は{収入|しゅうにゅう}が{安定|あんてい}しない。
examples.english: Day labor doesn't provide a stable income.

examples.japanese: {建設|けんせつ}{現場|げんば}では{日雇|ひやと}いの{労働者|ろうどうしゃ}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: There are many day laborers at construction sites.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}は{日雇|ひやと}いで{生計|せいけい}を{立|た}てていた。
examples.english: When I was young, I made a living doing day labor.

examples.japanese: {日雇|ひやと}い{労働者|ろうどうしゃ}の{権利|けんり}を{守|まも}る{法律|ほうりつ}が{整備|せいび}されてきた。
examples.english: Laws to protect the rights of day laborers have been developed.

examples.japanese: {戦後|せんご}の{大阪|おおさか}には{日雇|ひやと}いの{人|ひと}たちが{集|あつ}まる{地区|ちく}があった。
examples.english: In postwar Osaka, there were districts where day laborers gathered.

notes:
A compound of {日|ひ} (day) and {雇|やと}い (hiring). Can refer to either the work arrangement or the worker.

CULTURAL NOTE:
{日雇|ひやと}い{労働|ろうどう} has been a significant social issue in Japan. Areas like {釜|かま}ヶ{崎|さき} in Osaka and {山谷|さんや} in Tokyo were historically known as day laborer districts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日雇|ひやと}い{労働者|ろうどうしゃ} (day laborer)
- {日雇|ひやと}い{派遣|はけん} (daily temp work)
- {日雇|ひやと}いで{働|はたら}く (to work as a day laborer)
- {日雇|ひやと}いの{仕事|しごと} (day labor job)
